# dsh-subagent-mcp

**Give Codex a DeepSeek crew.** One tool call hands a task to a fresh DeepSeek Harness agent that
al

ready has your skills, your `AGENTS.md` and your sign-in — and it works in the project directory
you
name, then hands back the answer.
| What you get | Why it matters |
| **≈9k tokens per delegation** | A lite run costs about one file read, not a second conversation. |

| **V4.1-Flash at reasoning `max`** | The strong preset is the default. Nothing to tune. |
| **Your
skills and `AGENTS.md`** | It behaves like the DSH you configured, because it uses your `DSH_HOME`.

|
| **Long tasks can't be killed by a timeout** | It waits `wait_sec`, then returns a task id you c

ollect later. |
| **Zero runtime dependencies** | ~600 lines with a hand-rolled JSON-RPC loop. Nothi

ng to audit but the bridge. |
| **One process, one turn** | No daemon, no state to leak between task
s, no edits to your DSH profile. |
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Compared with other bridges in this space

Bridges between agent hosts and DeepSeek Harness come in three shapes: a **resident daemon** that
ke

eps agents alive and calls back into the host, an **SDK bridge** that runs workers in git
worktrees,

and a **relay** that exposes an already-running DSH instance. This package is the
fourth: a **state
less one-shot bridge**. Where it wins, and where it deliberately loses:
| Dimension | This package | Typical alternative | Why it matters |
| **Runtime dependencies** | **Zero** — only `dsh` itself | `ws` + `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` + `zo
d`, or a chain of SDK packages | A ~600-line single file is auditable in one sitting and cannot brea

k because a transitive dep changed |
| **Your DSH profile** | **Never touched** — config arrives as
`--patch` overlays | Written into the profile, or requires a plugin on the DSH side | Upgrading DSH

can't collide with a bridge that wrote itself into your config |
| **Per-call cost** | **Two explici
t tiers**: ≈9k or ≈300k tokens | One implicit size you discover on the bill | You choose the cost be

fore the run |
| **Lifetime** | One process per task, then exit | Resident daemon / worker pool | No

thing runs in the background; a crash can't poison the next task |
| **Orphan processes** | Process-
**tree** kill on cancel and shutdown | Sometimes leaves the MCP children `dsh` spawned | No slow mem

ory drain after a few cancelled runs |
| **Config inheritance** | Real `DSH_HOME` → your skills, `AG
ENTS.md`, sign-in | Some runtimes get an isolated temporary `DSH_HOME` (an empty shell) | The child

actually behaves like the DSH you configured |
| **Install** | `npx -y github:…`, no registry accoun

t | npm publish only | One config block, works today |
| **Cold start** | ≈1.7 s per delegation ⚠️ |

Warm daemon is faster | The honest price of statelessness |
| **Native callback / session attach**
| Not offered — needs host hooks ⚠️ | Daemon bridges call back natively and can attach to running se
ssions | If you need either, a daemon-shaped bridge is the right tool |
[该节后续省略]
## Install
Requires Node.js ≥ 22.19. The bundled dependency provides the `dsh` CLI.
**A · straight from GitHub** — no clone, no build, no npm account:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**B · pinned tarball**
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**C · clone** (when you want to read or patch the code)
[代码示例省略，未执行]
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Restart the host afterwards. Then just ask:
> Delegate to DSH: summarise `src/` and list the files that look unused. Work in `/path/to/project`.
## Tools
| Tool | Overlay | What it does |
| `subagent_dsh` | lite | Delegate a task: skills, shell, file editing, web search — no MCP tools. ≈

9k input tokens. |
| `subagent_dsh_full` | full | Same, plus every MCP server declared in `overlay.y

ml`. ≈300k input tokens with a dozen servers. |
| `subagent_dsh_status` | — | Collect a task. Accept

s a task id (`t-…`) **or** a dsh session id. |
| `subagent_dsh_continue` | — | Follow-up in the same

dsh session; `cwd`/`overlay` default to the remembered values. |
| `subagent_dsh_cancel` | — | Kill
a running or queued task and its whole process tree. |
| Argument | Default | Meaning |
| `prompt` | — | Required. The child cannot see the host conversation — include everything it needs.

|
| `cwd` | — | Required. Absolute project directory. **Not a sandbox** (see Security). |
| `wait_s

ec` | 120 | Wait before returning a task id. `0` returns immediately. |
| `timeout_sec` | 1800 | Har

d limit; on expiry the tree is killed and partial output returned. |
| `read_only` | false | Ask the

child to make no filesystem changes (instruction + detection, not a kernel sandbox). |
| `format` |
text | `json` returns `{ok, state, answer, usage, meta}`. |

Long tasks are safe by design: the call waits `wait_sec`, then returns a task id, so a host-side
too
l timeout can never kill the work.
## Model and cost

The child runs **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash** — model id `deepseek-flash` — at reasoning effort **max**.
Th
at is what both overlays ship; verify it yourself:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The account line exposes two ids (checked against `GET https://api.deepseek.com/models`):
| id | displayed as |

| `deepseek-flash` | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash · **default** |
| `deepseek-v4-pro` | DeepSeek-V4-Pro |
Switch per machine without editing files: `export DSH_SUBAGENT_MODEL=deepseek-v4-pro`.

> Pin the **id**, not the label. Provider-specific ids from other lines — for example opencode's
[该节

the **id**, not the label. Provider-specific ids from other lines — for example opencode's
[该节后续省略]
## Security

- **`cwd` is not a sandbox.** It selects the working directory only; the child inherits the host
use

r's filesystem and network rights.
- **`read_only` is advisory.** Enforced by instruction and report

ed by detection, not by the kernel.
- The child inherits `DSH_HOME`, so it reads your `AGENTS.md`, s

kills and stored credentials.
- Nothing is sent anywhere beyond the model provider you configured.
